/-!
# Erdős Problem 305

*References:*
- [erdosproblems.com/305](https://www.erdosproblems.com/305)
- [ErGr80] Erdős, P. and Graham, R., *Old and new problems and results in combinatorial number
  theory*. Monographies de L'Enseignement Mathematique (1980).
- [BlEr76] Bleicher, M. N. and Erdős, P., *Denominators of unit fractions*. J. Number Th. (1976),
  157-168.
- [Yo88] Yokota, H., *On a problem of Bleicher and Erdős*. J. Number Theory (1988), 198-207.
- [LiSa24] Liu, Y. and Sawhney, M., *On further questions regarding unit fractions*.
  arXiv:2404.07113 (2024).
-/

@[expose] public section

open Filter Real

namespace Erdos305

/--
`D a b` is the minimal value of $n_k$ such that there exist integers $1\leq n_1<\cdots <n_k$ with
$\frac{a}{b}=\frac{1}{n_1}+\cdots+\frac{1}{n_k}$.
-/
noncomputable def D (a b : ℕ) : ℕ :=
  sInf {B | ∃ E : Finset ℕ, 0 ∉ E ∧ (∀ n ∈ E, n ≤ B) ∧
    ∑ n ∈ E, (1 : ℚ) / n = a / b}

/-- $D(b)=\max_{1\leq a<b}D(a,b)$. -/
noncomputable def Dmax (b : ℕ) : ℕ := (Finset.Ico 1 b).sup fun a ↦ D a b

/--
For integers $1\leq a<b$ let $D(a,b)$ be the minimal value of $n_k$ such that there exist
integers $1\leq n_1<\cdots <n_k$ with
$$\frac{a}{b}=\frac{1}{n_1}+\cdots+\frac{1}{n_k}.$$
Estimate $D(b)=\max_{1\leq a<b}D(a,b)$. Is it true that
$$D(b) \ll b(\log b)^{1+o(1)}?$$

Bleicher and Erdős [BlEr76] have shown that $D(b)\ll b(\log b)^2$. If $b=p$ is a prime then
$D(p) \gg p\log p$.

This was solved by Yokota [Yo88], who proved that
$$D(b)\ll b(\log b)(\log\log b)^4(\log\log\log b)^2.$$
This was improved by Liu and Sawhney [LiSa24] to
$$D(b)\ll b(\log b)(\log\log b)^3(\log\log\log b)^{O(1)}.$$
-/
@[category research solved, AMS 11, formal_proof using lean4 at
  "https://github.com/plby/lean-proofs/blob/8822f7ddef30fadbd92e1c6ab4ed897af356af5e/src/latest/ErdosProblems/Erdos305.lean#L217"]
theorem erdos_305 : answer(True) ↔ ∃ δ : ℕ → ℝ, Tendsto δ atTop (nhds 0) ∧
    ∃ C : ℝ, 0 < C ∧ ∀ᶠ b : ℕ in atTop,
      (Dmax b : ℝ) ≤ C * b * (log b) ^ (1 + δ b) := by
  sorry

/-- Bleicher and Erdős [BlEr76] have shown that $D(b)\ll b(\log b)^2$. -/
@[category research solved, AMS 11]
theorem erdos_305.variants.bleicher_erdos : ∃ C : ℝ, 0 < C ∧
    ∀ᶠ b : ℕ in atTop, (Dmax b : ℝ) ≤ C * b * (log b) ^ 2 := by
  sorry

/-- If $b=p$ is a prime then $D(p) \gg p\log p$. -/
@[category research solved, AMS 11]
theorem erdos_305.variants.prime_lower_bound : ∃ c : ℝ, 0 < c ∧
    ∀ᶠ p : ℕ in atTop, p.Prime → c * p * log p ≤ Dmax p := by
  sorry

/--
Yokota [Yo88] proved that $D(b)\ll b(\log b)(\log\log b)^4(\log\log\log b)^2$.
-/
@[category research solved, AMS 11]
theorem erdos_305.variants.yokota : ∃ C : ℝ, 0 < C ∧ ∀ᶠ b : ℕ in atTop,
    (Dmax b : ℝ) ≤ C * b * log b * log (log b) ^ 4 * log (log (log b)) ^ 2 := by
  sorry

/--
Liu and Sawhney [LiSa24] proved that $D(b)\ll b(\log b)(\log\log b)^3(\log\log\log b)^{O(1)}$.
-/
@[category research solved, AMS 11]
theorem erdos_305.variants.liu_sawhney : ∃ C K : ℝ, 0 < C ∧ ∀ᶠ b : ℕ in atTop,
    (Dmax b : ℝ) ≤ C * b * log b * log (log b) ^ 3 * log (log (log b)) ^ K := by
  sorry

end Erdos305

findings.description: The shared [BlEr76] reference points to the Journal of Number Theory paper, pp. 157–168, but the main theorem's docstring and `Erdos305.erdos_305.variants.bleicher_erdos` cite it for D(b) ≪ b(log b)^2. That paper's Theorem 2 gives the cubic-log bound. The squared-log bound is proved in the separate paper Denominators of Egyptian fractions II. This is a citation slip, also present on the problem webpage, not an error in the Lean statements.
findings.source_evidence: Bleicher–Erdős, Denominators of Egyptian fractions, J. Number Theory 8 (1976), Theorem 2, pp. 162–163, states D(N) < K N(ln N)^3: https://www.renyi.hu/~p_erdos/1976-09.pdf. Their Denominators of Egyptian fractions II, Illinois J. Math. 20 (1976), Theorem 1, p. 602, establishes D(N) ≪ N(log N)^2: https://combinatorica.hu/~p_erdos/1976-10.pdf.
findings.suggested_fix: Add a separate reference to Denominators of Egyptian fractions II, Illinois J. Math. 20 (1976), 598–613, and cite it for the squared-log bound in both docstrings. Retain the first paper for the prime lower bound, correcting its title to Denominators of Egyptian fractions. No Lean statement needs changing.

reformulations.difference: The original conjecture in Erdős–Graham, p. 38, and Bleicher–Erdős, Conjecture 3, uses a bound with exponent 1+ε for every ε>0 and a constant depending on ε. Lean instead uses one function δ(b)→0 and one positive multiplicative constant, expressing the webpage's 1+o(1) formulation.
reformulations.equivalence_argument: From Lean's formulation, for each ε>0 eventually δ(b)≤ε and log b≥1, giving the ε-bound. Finitely many remaining b≥2 can be absorbed into its constant. Conversely, choose bounds for ε=1/m and increasing thresholds N_m large enough that their constants are at most (log b)^(1/m) for b≥N_m. Then D(b)≤b(log b)^(1+2/m) beyond N_m. Taking δ(b)=2/m for the largest eligible m gives δ(b)→0 and a single constant, even C=1.

reformulations.difference: The O(1) exponent is represented by a fixed real K, without an explicit nonnegativity condition.
reformulations.equivalence_argument: The iterated logarithm log(log(log b)) tends to infinity, so it is eventually at least 1, and the other factors are eventually nonnegative. Any real K can therefore be replaced by a natural number N≥K without invalidating the upper bound. Conversely, a natural exponent is a real exponent. A bounded exponent function, as in O(1), is likewise dominated by a fixed exponent. The real-exponent/natural-exponent equivalence was proved in /workspace/review/asymptotics.lean.

review.notes: All seven mathematical declarations were checked. Rational coercions are correct; positive fractions have expansions, so the natural-number infimum is attained rather than defaulting to zero. Finite sets correctly encode distinct denominators, and all logarithmic edge cases are excluded by eventual quantification. Kernel-checked boundary tests include D(2,3)=6 and Dmax(4)=4. The exact linked proof and its 46 local dependencies rebuilt successfully; its axiom list is [propext, Classical.choice, Quot.sound]. /workspace/review/bridge.lean independently proves the repository's exact main statement from those dependencies, with the same axiom list.
